I'm an Android phone user and part of the internals is setup so that if you turn on automatic backup of your photos to Google Photos in the cloud, once the photo is backed up, a little icon is placed on the edge of the photo on your phone letting you know that it has been successfully backed up to the cloud. At that point, if you have Media Management Apps/Allow app to manage media ENABLED for PHOTOS AND you enable Storage Manager under the Storage settings, Google will automatically REMOVE FROM YOUR PHONE OR TABLET devices any photos and videos that have been successfully backed up to the google photos cloud. It does this to help keep your phone memory available to continue receiving mail, etc. This generally means that you don't have to manually purge your phone of backed up photos. Once photos reach 90 days old on your phone, they are automatically removed from your phone, but the backup copies are always there that you can see simply by opening Google Photos on your phone, tablet or PC.
